content.text: Lrg effusion w.in hrs of trauma: hemarthrosis -ACL/fx
varus: medial OA; valgus: lat OA
- Effusion: present: intra-articular pathology/synovitis     -     Irregular bony ridges along joint margins: osteophytes: OA
A. knee:         - tibial tuberosity            - tibiofemoral joint
Medial & lat joint space:          - medial/lat tibial plateau
- medial/lat femoral condyle   - medial/lat menisci     - MCL, LCL
Extend: loss/lag: extensor-mech disruption or locked meniscus
Hyperextend (ROM only): genu recurvatum: ligamentous laxity
extend:   weak: quad/patellar tendon (L3–L4)                         unable to SLR: extensor rupture
Knee extend, ↓P on suprapatellar pouch w 1 hand, tap patella against femur w other hand
Detects lrg effusions than bulge sign.
Knee extended, milk down from suprapatellar recess, apply medial P, tap bulge on lateral side
Grasp leg w both hands, thumbs at tibial plateau, fingers behind calf, pull tibia forward
Lachman is more sensitive than A. drawer
Grasp upper calf, thumb over A. joint line, stabilize femur, pull tibia A.in sudden forward
supine, flex knee w foot flat on table (stabilize )
- grasp leg w both hands, thumbs on tibial plateau/joint line, push tibia P.(backward)
Check for P. sag at 90° first
inward P at thigh, outward at ankle
Laxity in full extend: more severe injury
outward P medial thigh, inward P from lat ankle
Laxity in full extend: more severe injury.
pt on belly, knee flexed at 90’, ↓P on heel of foot & IR/ER lower leg
: 1 hand lat meniscus, 1 holds foot & IR foot -> varus knee stress & slowly extend
: 1 hand medial meniscus, 1 holds foot, ER foot -> valgus knee  stress &  slowly extend
pt seated or supine, w affected leg extended at knee, supported on exam table
- ask pt to lift leg straight up w.o holding leg
